speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me understand the issue, could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of falling on your outstretched hand six months ago, combined with pain radiating to the elbow and worsening with lifting your infant, raises concern for an occult fracture or ligament injury that may have been missed. Did you notice any swelling, bruising, or tenderness directly over the wrist joint or the base of your thumb at the time of the fall or currently?

speaker: Patient
text: patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fall six months ago is a significant risk for a scaphoid fracture, but your pain worsening with lifting an infant also strongly suggests De Quervain's tenosynovitis or carpal tunnel syndrome. Can you tell me if you have any numbness or tingling in your thumb and index finger, and does tilting your head to the side toward the painful wrist make the pain worse?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previous fall on right outstretched hand six months ago. No significant other medical history. Social history: Patient is a mother of an infant, leading a relatively active lifestyle. Does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scaphoid fracture with delayed union.

The history of a fall on an outstretched hand six months ago, persisting pain in the anatomical snuffbox area, and symptoms worsening with lifting are classic for a missed scaphoid fracture. I need to confirm this with imaging.
